# Sloppy or Not

> Sloppy or Not is a free, educational tool that tells you whether a website, app, or software project built with AI is sloppy or not. You paste a live link and get one word back: Sloppy or Not. No number is ever shown to anyone.

Sloppy or Not was built in Charleston, SC, at HarborHacks, the Agent in the Loop hackathon hosted by Charleston Hacks, by AI Tech Girlfriends: Therese Grittner (agent intelligence, pitch, and demo; TaG Makes, https://tagmakessc.com), Olivia Dennehy (design, frontend, and UX), and Jacky Schuler (backend, storage, and agent runtime).

How a project is judged:

- Measured checks come first: whether the page loads, page speed, accessibility, whether it works on a phone, basic security headers, and errors. A site that does not load is Sloppy.
- Dot, the Sloppy or Not agent, answers six questions from the live site, such as whether a stranger can tell what it does from the first screen and whether its claims match the page.
- The builder can answer nine questions about their thinking, written by designer Olivia Dennehy. Good answers can rescue a borderline site. They cannot rescue a broken one. Dot never writes these answers.
- Swipes from other people feed the weekly State of Slop email and never change a verdict.
- A project's first verdict is saved. Resubmitting the same link does not change it.
- Verdicts are not published unless the builder opts in with "Roast me."

Sloppy or Not also feeds Gituationship, where a persistent agent finds what a good product is missing, proposes a partner product that fills the gap, and waits for a human to approve every match.

## Pages

- [Home](https://sloppyornot.com/): what Sloppy or Not is and how to start.
- [How we judge](https://sloppyornot.com/criteria): the measured checks, Dot's six questions, and the nine builder questions.
- [About](https://sloppyornot.com/about): the project, who it is for, credits, and the privacy policy.
- [Enter your project](https://sloppyornot.com/submit): submit a live link and get a verdict.
- [Judge projects](https://sloppyornot.com/judge): swipe on other people's projects, left for slop and right for not.

## Optional

- [Source code](https://github.com/tagmakes-maker/sloppyornot): the site, the worker API, the agent prompts, and the scoring rules.
